title: Rajasthan Judiciary Prelims Question Bank
sourceNote: Based on the supplied Law Mock prelims-2015.pdf and prelims-2017.pdf, with 85 questions from each source. Years and question numbers are the labels printed in the supplied editions. The PDFs are partial and have no Hindi section. Explanations and answer letters come from the PDFs. Records requiring review retain their printed answer letter in the note and are unscored. Historical law and case questions should be read in their exam context.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Agricultural Credit
questions.question: Under the provisions of the Rajasthan Agricultural Credit Operations (Removal of difficulties) Act, 1974, a Bank can recover its dues from any agriculturist or his heir or legal representative or his guarantor on account of financial assistance availed of by the agriculturist by making an application to:
options: District Judge
High Court
Prescribed Authority
None of the above
questions.explanation: Under the Rajasthan Agricultural Credit Operations (Removal of Difficulties) Act, 1974, a Bank recovers its dues by applying to the Prescribed Authority, which then certifies the amount for recovery as arrears of land revenue.
questions.reference: Rajasthan Agricultural Credit Operations (Removal of Difficulties) Act, 1974

questions.subject: Rajasthan Court Fees
questions.question: Under Section 35 of the Rajasthan court Fees and suits valuation Act, 1961, in a suit for partition and separate possession of a share in joint family property by a plaintiff, who has been excluded from possession of such property, court fee shall be:-
options: paid at fixed rate
computed on the market value of the plaintiff's share of the property
at the discretion of the plaintiff
based on written statement of the defendant
questions.explanation: Section 35 of the Rajasthan Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1961, provides that where a plaintiff excluded from possession sues for partition and separate possession of his share of joint family property, court fee is computed on the market value of the plaintiff's share.
questions.reference: Rajasthan Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1961, Section 35

questions.subject: Rajasthan Stamp Act
questions.question: Under the Rajasthan Stamp Act, 1998, in case of a release-deed, in the absence of an agreement to the contrary, the expense of providing the proper stamp shall be borne by:
options: the beneficiary
the person drawing, making or executing the release-deed
by both the parties in equal shares
none of the above
questions.explanation: Mirroring Section 29 of the Indian Stamp Act, under the Rajasthan Stamp Act, 1998, in the case of a release-deed, absent contrary agreement, the duty/expense of providing the proper stamp is borne by the person drawing, making or executing the instrument.
questions.reference: Rajasthan Stamp Act, 1998 (see provision governing who bears stamp duty)

questions.subject: Rajasthan Stamp Act
questions.question: If an instrument has not been duly stamped and where such an instrument has been admitted in evidence, such admission:
options: can be called in question at any stage of the same suit or proceeding
not be called in question at any stage of the same suit or proceeding except as provided for by Section 71 of the Rajasthan Stamp Act, 1998
at the discretion of the opposite party can be called in question
none of the above
questions.explanation: Like Section 36 of the Indian Stamp Act, once an instrument has been admitted in evidence, such admission cannot be called in question at any stage of the same suit or proceeding except as provided (here, Section 71 of the Rajasthan Stamp Act, 1998).
questions.reference: Rajasthan Stamp Act, 1998 (admission of instruments), read with Section 71

questions.subject: Registration
questions.question: Under the Registration Act, 1908 a will can be presented for registration before the Registrar or Sub Registrar by:
options: the testator
after death of testator, any person claiming as executor or otherwise under a will
both (a) and (b)
none of the above
questions.explanation: Under Section 40 of the Registration Act, 1908, a will may be presented for registration by the testator himself, or after his death by any person claiming as executor or otherwise under the will; hence both (a) and (b).

questions.subject: Contract Law
questions.question: Two parties entered into a contract. They later realised that the law as they understood as applicable was not in force in India. This makes their contract:
options: illegal
void
voidable
none of the above
questions.explanation: An agreement made under a mutual mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement is void under Section 20 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872; a mistaken belief about a law not in force in India is treated as a mistake of fact, rendering the contract void.

questions.subject: Limitation
questions.question: Acknowledgement after the expiration of the period prescribed under the Indian Limitation Act, 1963, for a suit or application:
options: is of no effect
gives rise to an independent & enforceable contract
is of great value
none of the above
questions.explanation: A promise to pay a time-barred debt is enforceable; an acknowledgement/promise after expiry of the limitation period gives rise to an independent and enforceable contract (cf. Section 25(3) Contract Act). Acknowledgement under Section 18 of the Limitation Act only extends time if made before expiry.
questions.reference: Limitation Act, 1963, Section 18; Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 25(3)
questions.note: The explanation conflates an acknowledgment with a signed promise to pay a time-barred debt. PDF answer key: B.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Rent Control
questions.question: Time limit for disposal of a petition filed under Section 9 of Rajasthan Rent Control Act, 2001 is:-
options: the period of two hundred and forty days from the date of service of notice on the tenant
within the period of twelve months from the date of service of notice on the tenant
within the period of six months from the date of service of notice on the tenant
no limitation
questions.explanation: A petition under the Rajasthan Rent Control Act, 2001 is to be disposed of within two hundred and forty (240) days from the date of service of notice on the tenant.
questions.reference: Rajasthan Rent Control Act, 2001, Sections 9 and 15

questions.subject: Partnership
questions.question: Subject to contract between the partners, a firm is dissolved:
options: if constituted for a fixed term, by the expiry of that term
if constituted to carry out one or more adventures or undertakings, by the completion thereof
by the death of a partner
all the above
questions.explanation: Under Section 42 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (subject to contract between partners), a firm is dissolved by expiry of a fixed term, by completion of the adventures/undertakings, and by the death of a partner; hence all the above.

questions.subject: Contract Law
questions.question: Finder of lost goods under Indian contract Act, 1872 is a:
options: bailor
surety
bailee
none of the above
questions.explanation: Under Section 71 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the finder of lost goods is in the position of a bailee, with the responsibilities of a bailee.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Right to Hearing
questions.question: Under Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act, 2012, a complaint can be filed regarding grievance relating to:
options: the service matters of a public servant
any matter in which any Court or Tribunal has jurisdiction
any matter under Right to Information Act, 2005
none of the above
questions.explanation: The Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act, 2012 expressly excludes service matters of public servants, matters within the jurisdiction of any court/tribunal, and RTI matters; therefore none of (a)-(c) is a maintainable grievance.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In which of the following cases has the Supreme Court ruled that the members of the Transgender Community who are neither male nor female, at the time of birth, are recognized as 'Third Gender' for the purpose of safeguarding and enforcing appropriately their fundamental and other legal, social and economic rights guaranteed under the constitution?
options: Rambilas singh vs. State of Bihar - AIR 1989 SC 1593
Lily Thomas Vs. Union of India - (2013) 7 SCC 653
National Legal Services Authority vs. Union of India - (2014) 5 SCC 438
None of the above
questions.explanation: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India, (2014) 5 SCC 438 (NALSA), is the case in which the Supreme Court recognised transgender persons as a 'third gender' and protected their constitutional rights.
questions.reference: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India, (2014) 5 SCC 438

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 21-A providing for Right to Education was inserted in the constitution by:
options: the Constitution (Eighty Sixth Amendment) Act, 2002
the Constitution (Ninety First Amendment) Act, 2003
the Constitution (Ninety Second Amendment) Act, 2003
the constitution (Eighty Fourth Amendment) Act, 2001
questions.explanation: Article 21-A (Right to Education) was inserted by the Constitution (Eighty-Sixth Amendment) Act, 2002.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct statement in so far as Section 20 of the Code of civil Procedure, 1908, is concerned?
options: The suit has to be instituted in the court of the lowest grade competent to try it
The suit has to be instituted in the court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the defendant actually and voluntarily resides or carries on business or personally works for gain
The suit has to be instituted in the court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction, the cause of action wholly or in part arises
All the above are correct
questions.explanation: Section 20 CPC permits suit where the defendant resides/carries on business (option b) or where the cause of action wholly or in part arises (option c); the 'lowest grade competent' rule is Section 15. Read with the framing, all the listed propositions are recognised principles, so 'all the above'.
questions.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Sections 15 and 20
questions.note: The keyed all-of-the-above answer includes a proposition the solution attributes to Section 15, while the question asks about Section 20. PDF answer key: D.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: In which of the following cases, did the Supreme Court uphold the validity of the code of civil Procedure Amendment Acts of 1999 and 2002?
options: Delhi H.C. Bar Association Vs. UOI
Allahabad H.C. Bar Association Vs. VOI
Salem Advocate Bar Association Vs. UOI
P & H H.C. Bar Association Vs. UOI
questions.explanation: In Salem Advocate Bar Association v. Union of India, the Supreme Court upheld the validity of the CPC (Amendment) Acts of 1999 and 2002.
questions.reference: Salem Advocate Bar Association v. Union of India (CPC amendments)

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: An Appeal under Order XLIII of Code of Civil Procedure shall lie from which of the following orders:
options: Rule-11 of Order VII, rejecting the plaint
Rule-9 of order XXII, refusing to set aside the abatement or dismissal of suit
Rule-1 of order VIII, not permitting the defendant to present the written statement
Rule-5 of Order XIV, refusing to strike out the issue at the instance of either of the parties
questions.explanation: Order XLIII Rule 1 CPC lists appealable orders, including an order under Order XXII Rule 9 refusing to set aside an abatement or dismissal of a suit. Rejection of plaint (Order VII Rule 11) is a decree, not an Order XLIII appeal.
questions.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order XLIII Rule 1, Order XXII Rule 9, Order VII Rule 11

questions.subject: Easements
questions.question: Statement 'A' - where the access and use of light or air to and for any building have been peaceably enjoyed therewith, as an easement, without interruption, and for twenty years, the right to such access and use of light or air shall be absolute. Statement 'B' - A right to the free passage of light or air to an open space of ground, cannot be acquired by prescription.
options: 'A' is correct
statement 'B' is correct
Both statements are correct
Both statements are incorrect
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: Section 25 of the Indian Easements Act, 1882 grants an absolute right to light/air enjoyed peaceably for 20 years (Statement A), while the Explanation/settled law denies prescriptive right to free passage of light or air to an open space of ground (Statement B).

questions.subject: Specific Relief
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: In a suit for specific performance of a contract for transfer of immovable property, the court cannot grant partition and separate possession of the property
In a suit for specific performance of a contract for transfer of immovable property, the plaintiff cannot alternatively ask for the refund of earnest money or deposit made by him
The court while refusing to grant specific performance of the contract, cannot grant refund of earnest money paid by the plaintiff, unless it has been specifically claimed
All the above are correct
questions.explanation: In a suit for specific performance of a contract to transfer immovable property, the court cannot grant partition and separate possession of the property; (b) and (c) are wrong because a plaintiff may alternatively claim, and the court may grant, refund of earnest money/deposit (Sections 21-22 Specific Relief Act).
questions.note: The keyed restriction on partition and separate possession needs checking against Section 22 and the actual choices. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: Registration
questions.question: Which of the following documents is not required to be compulsorily registered ?
options: Instruments creating or declaring right, title or interest to or in immovable property of rupees one hundred and upwards
wills in respect of immovable property
Leases of immovable property for a term exceeding one year
Instruments transferring any decree of a court when such decree purports to create right in immovable property of rupees one hundred and upwards
questions.explanation: Under Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908, wills are expressly exempt from compulsory registration (their registration is optional under Section 18); the instruments in (a), (c) and (d) are compulsorily registrable.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: In which of the following mortgages, the mortgagor is required to deliver possession of the mortgaged property to the mortgagee?
options: English mortgage
Mortgage by conditional sale
Usufructuary mortgage
Anomalous mortgage
questions.explanation: In a usufructuary mortgage (Section 58(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882), the mortgagor delivers possession of the mortgaged property to the mortgagee, who retains possession and receives rents/profits in lieu of interest/principal.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Statement 'A' - Every transfer of immovable property made with intent to defeat or delay the creditors of the transferor is void. Statement 'B' - Every transfer of immovable property made without consideration with intent to defraud a subsequent transferee is void.
options: statement 'A' is correct
Statement 'B' is correct
Both statements are correct
Both statements are incorrect
questions.explanation: Both statements are incorrect: under Section 53 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, such transfers (to defeat/delay creditors, or without consideration to defraud a subsequent transferee) are voidable at the option of the person defeated/defrauded, not void.

questions.subject: Arbitration
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct, so far as Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is concerned?
options: A party may apply to the court for interim measures during the pendency of the arbitration proceedings only
A party may apply to the court seeking appointment of receiver by way of interim measures even after the making of the arbitral award by the Arbitral Tribunal
A party cannot apply for interim measures before the commencement of arbitral proceedings
All the above are correct
questions.explanation: Under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, a party may seek interim measures (e.g., appointment of a receiver) before, during, and even after the making of the arbitral award (but before enforcement); statements (a) and (c) wrongly restrict this, so (b) is the correct statement.

questions.subject: Limitation
questions.question: The period of three years is prescribed under Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963, in case where no other period of Limitation is provided for filing any:-
options: suit
Appeal
Application
Proceeding
questions.explanation: Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963 is the residuary article prescribing three years for any application for which no period of limitation is provided elsewhere in the Schedule.

questions.subject: Limitation
questions.question: Statement 'A' - In computing the period of limitation for any appeal, the day from which such period is to be reckoned, shall be included. Statement 'B' - In computing period of Limitation for any appeal, the day on which the judgement complained of was pronounced and the time requisite for obtaining the copy of the decree shall be excluded.
options: statement 'A' is correct
statement 'B' is correct
Both are correct
Both are incorrect
questions.explanation: Statement B is correct: under Sections 12(1) and 12(2) of the Limitation Act, 1963, in computing limitation for an appeal, the day of pronouncement of the judgment and the time requisite for obtaining the copy of the decree are excluded; Statement A is wrong because that day is excluded, not included.

questions.subject: Legal Services Authorities Act
questions.question: Which of the following is correct as per Section 22-c of the Legal Services Authority Act, 1987?
options: Any party to a dispute may, after the dispute is brought before any court, make an application to the Permanent Lok Adalat for the settlement of dispute
The Permanent Lok Adalat shall not have the jurisdiction in respect of any matter relating to an offence not compoundable under any law
The Permanent Lok Adalat shall have the jurisdiction only in such matter where the value of the property in dispute is more than ten lakh rupees
All the above are correct
questions.explanation: Under Section 22-C of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, the Permanent Lok Adalat has no jurisdiction over any matter relating to an offence not compoundable under any law. Option (a) is wrong (application must be made 'before' the dispute goes to court) and (c) is wrong (PLA has no jurisdiction where property value 'exceeds' ten lakh rupees).

questions.subject: Hindu Law
questions.question: Under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the marriage may be declared null and void if:
options: the parties are within the degrees of prohibited relationship
at the time of the marriage, one of the parties was incapable of giving a valid consent to it in consequence of unsoundness of mind
at the time of the marriage, one of the parties was subject to recurrent attacks of insanity
in all the above circumstances
questions.explanation: Section 11 HMA, 1955 makes a marriage null and void only for breach of Section 5 clauses (i) bigamy, (iv) prohibited degrees and (v) sapinda. Of the listed options, parties within prohibited degrees (a) is a void ground; unsoundness of mind and recurrent insanity (b, c) are voidable grounds under Section 12(1)(b), so (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Hindu Law
questions.question: After the Hindu succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, the daughter of a coparcener in a Joint Hindu family governed by the Mitakshara law:
options: shall have no right in the coparcenary property
cannot become a coparcener by birth
shall become a coparcener by birth in her own right in the same manner as the son
shall be entitled to dispose of the entire coparcenary property
questions.explanation: Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act as amended by the 2005 Amendment makes the daughter of a coparcener a coparcener by birth in her own right in the same manner as the son.

questions.subject: Hindu Law
questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect?
options: The husband is the natural guardian of a Hindu married girl
After the adoption of Hindu minor son, his father continues to remain his natural guardian till he attains majority
The natural guardian of a Hindu minor child is the father, and after him the mother, but custody of minor up to the age of five years shall ordinarily be with the mother
The natural guardian of an illegitimate Hindu minor boy is the mother, and after her, the father
questions.explanation: Under the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, on adoption of a Hindu minor the natural guardianship vests in the adoptive parents; the natural father does NOT continue as natural guardian. Hence statement (b) is incorrect. (Statements (a), (c) and (d) correctly state Section 6.)
questions.reference: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, Sections 6 and 7

questions.subject: Hindu Law
questions.question: A Hindu wife is entitled to claim maintenance after the death of her husband from her father-in-law under:
options: Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
Section 19 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956
Section 10 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
questions.explanation: Section 19 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 entitles a Hindu widow to be maintained, after her husband's death, by her father-in-law (out of coparcenary property/estate).
questions.reference: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, Section 19

questions.subject: Domestic Violence Act
questions.question: As per section 2(q) of the Protection of women from Domestic violence Act, 2005, "respondent" means and includes:
options: any person, who is in a domestic relationship with the aggrieved person and against whom the aggrieved person has sought relief under the Act
male partner when aggrieved female is living in a relationship with him in the nature of a marriage
the female relatives of the husband of the aggrieved wife, seeking their removal from the shared household
none of the above
questions.explanation: Section 2(q) of the PWDV Act, 2005 defines 'respondent' as any adult person who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the aggrieved person and against whom relief is sought under the Act.
questions.reference: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Section 2(q)
questions.note: The option and explanation differ on the wording of the historical definition. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Rent Control
questions.question: As per section 3 of the Rajasthan Rent control Act, 2001, the chapter II and III thereof do not apply to:
options: the premises, let out after the commencement of the Act for a period of two years through a registered deed
the premises, let out to the multinational company having paid up share capital of less than rupees one crore
the premises, let out for residential purposes, the monthly rent whereof is rupees four thousand in case of the premises situated in the Municipal area of Jaipur city
the premises belonging to the Government company as defined under the Companies Act, 1956
questions.explanation: Section 3 of the Rajasthan Rent Control Act, 2001 exempts (inter alia) premises belonging to the Government and to a Government company as defined under the Companies Act, 1956 from the application of Chapters II and III.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Tenancy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is not correct, so far as Section 242 of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955 is concerned?
options: civil court can frame the issue with regard to the tenancy rights in agricultural land and submit the record to the appropriate revenue court for the decision on that issue only
civil court may or may not accept the finding of revenue court on the issue referred to it
The finding of the revenue court on the issue referred to it, shall be deemed to be part of the finding of civil court for the purposes of Appeal
civil court cannot decide the issue which was referred to the revenue cour
questions.explanation: Under Section 242 of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955, the civil court refers the tenancy issue to the revenue court and is bound by that finding; it is not free to accept or reject it. Hence statement (b) is the one that is NOT correct.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Land Revenue
questions.question: Which of the following is not the judicial matter under Section 23 read with the First schedule to the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956?
options: Regularisation of unauthorised occupation
A dispute with respect to the right of grazing cattle on pasture land
Settlement of boundary disputes
Mutation upon succession
questions.explanation: Under Section 23 read with the First Schedule of the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956, 'judicial matters' are adjudicatory proceedings (boundary disputes, grazing-right disputes, regularisation). Routine mutation upon succession is an administrative/non-judicial matter, so (d) is not a judicial matter.

questions.subject: Rajasthan General Rules (Civil)
questions.question: The General Rules (Civil), 1986 have been framed:
options: by the Rajasthan High Court under Article 227 of the constitution of India
by the Governor under Article 166 of the Constitution of India
by the Chief Justice under Article 229 of the Constitution of India.
by the State Government under Article 309 of the Constitution of India
questions.explanation: The General Rules (Civil), 1986 are framed by the Rajasthan High Court in exercise of its power of superintendence over subordinate courts under Article 227 of the Constitution.
questions.reference: Rajasthan General Rules (Civil), 1986; Constitution of India, Article 227

questions.subject: Muslim Law
questions.question: Which of the followings is not an essential ingredient of gift under the Mohammedan law :
options: a declaration of gift by the donor
acceptance of gift, expressed or implied, by or on behalf of donee
delivery of possession of the subject gift by the donor to the donee
a written deed of gift
questions.explanation: Under Mohammedan law the three essentials of a valid hiba (gift) are declaration, acceptance and delivery of possession. A written/registered deed is NOT essential, so (d) is the non-essential.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following is correct statement of law as per sections 82 and 83 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973?
options: The court may order attachment of property belonging to an accused before declaring him a proclaimed person under Section 82
The court may order attachment of property of a person after publication of a written proclamation under Section 82 requiring him to appear before it
The court may order attachment of property of a person regardless of whether or not he has been declared proclaimed offender
None of the above
questions.explanation: Under Sections 82-83 CrPC, attachment of property under Section 83 may be ordered only after publication of the written proclamation under Section 82 requiring the person to appear.
questions.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Sections 82-83, Section 83, Section 82
questions.note: Check the answer against the proviso governing simultaneous attachment under Section 83. PDF answer key: B.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following irregularities of a Magistrate, not empowered by law to do so, vitiates the proceedings?
options: To hold inquiry under Section 176 code of criminal procedure
To make over a case under Sub-Section (2) of Section 192 code of criminal procedure
To take cognizance of an offence under clause (c) of subsection (1) of Section 190 of the code of criminal procedure
To tender pardon to accomplice under Section 306 of the code of criminal procedure
questions.explanation: Under Section 461(k) CrPC, taking cognizance of an offence under clause (c) of Section 190(1) by a Magistrate not empowered to do so vitiates the proceedings; the others (inquiry u/s 176, making over u/s 192(2), tender of pardon u/s 306) are curable under Section 460.
questions.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Section 461(k), Section 190(1), Section 460

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following irregularities of a Magistrate not empowered by Taw to do so, does not vitiate the proceedings:
options: calling of record to exercise powers of revision under Section 397 of Code of Criminal Procedure
taking cognizance of an offence under clause (a) or clause (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 190 of Code of Criminal Procedure
decision of an appeal
revision of an order passed under section 466 of Code of Criminal Procedure
questions.explanation: Under Section 460(e) CrPC, taking cognizance under clause (a) or (b) of Section 190(1) by a Magistrate not empowered, if done in good faith, does NOT vitiate the proceedings. Revision, deciding an appeal and revising an order u/s 466 are incurable irregularities under Section 461.
questions.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Section 460(e), Section 190(1), Section 461

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following offences is cognizable, non-bailable and non compoundable:
options: voluntarily causing grievous hurt, punishable under Section 325 IPC
attempt to murder punishable under Section 307 IPC
voluntarily causing hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property, punishable under Section 330 IPC
voluntarily causing grievous hurt on provocation punishable under Section 335 IPC
questions.explanation: Attempt to murder under Section 307 IPC is cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable. Section 325 (s.323-compoundable category) and 335 are compoundable; the others do not meet all three conditions as cleanly as 307.
questions.reference: Indian Penal Code, Section 307; CrPC, First Schedule and Section 320

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: Which of the following provisions of the Indian Penal Code defines culpable homicide
options: Section 302
Section 300
Section 301
Section 299
questions.explanation: Section 299 IPC defines culpable homicide; Section 300 defines murder, and Sections 301/302 deal with consequences/punishment.
questions.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860, Section 299, Section 300, Sections 301

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Statement of an accused can be recorded on oath:
options: is not a correct statement of law
under Section 315 code of criminal procedure
under Section 313 code of criminal procedure
under Section 391 code of criminal procedure
questions.explanation: Under Section 313(2) CrPC no oath is administered to the accused when examined; and as a witness u/s 315 the accused gives evidence on oath only on his own request in defence - there is no general rule that an accused's statement is recorded on oath, so (a) 'is not a correct statement of law' is correct.

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct statement according to law?
options: An accomplice shall be competent witness against an accused person
Leading question may be asked in cross-examination of a witness
The court may permit a party, who, calls a witness, to put any question to him, which might be put in cross examination by the adverse party
All the above
questions.explanation: All are correct: an accomplice is a competent witness (Section 133 Evidence Act); leading questions are permitted in cross-examination (Section 143); and the court may permit a party to put cross-examination-type questions to its own witness (Section 154, hostile witness).
questions.reference: Indian Evidence Act, 1872, Section 133, Section 143, Section 154

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: Burden of proof under Section 101 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872:
options: goes on shifting as the trial proceeds
never shifts
may shift
both (a) and (c) are correct
questions.explanation: Section 101 of the Evidence Act lays down the burden of proof on the party who asserts; this legal/persuasive burden never shifts (it is the onus of proof under s.102 that shifts).

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Proceedings under section 145 of the code of criminal Procedure are initiated by the Executive Magistrate on the report of which of the following?
options: Judicial Magistrate
Police officer
Revenue officer
Complainant
questions.explanation: Proceedings under Section 145 CrPC are initiated by the Executive Magistrate on being satisfied from a police officer's report or other information of a dispute likely to cause breach of peace.

questions.subject: Negotiable Instruments
questions.question: In which of the following judgments has the Supreme Court held that only those courts within whose territorial limits the drawee bank is situated, would have jurisdiction to try the cases for offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881?
options: K. Bhaskaran vs. Sankaran vaidhyan Balan and Another - (1999) 7 SCC 510
Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod vs. State of Maharashtra and Another - (2014) 9 SCC 129
state of Bihar and others vs. Kalyan pur cement Limited - (2010) 3 SCC 274
None of the above
questions.explanation: In Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod v. State of Maharashtra, (2014) 9 SCC 129, the Supreme Court held that only the court within whose territorial jurisdiction the drawee bank (where the cheque is dishonoured) is situated has jurisdiction to try a Section 138 NI Act offence.
questions.reference: Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod v. State of Maharashtra, (2014) 9 SCC 129; NI Act, Sections 138 and 142
questions.note: Historical case-law question. The 2015 amendments changed the statutory framework for territorial jurisdiction.

questions.subject: Negotiable Instruments
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct statement of law as per Sections 138 and 142 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881?
options: A cheque is to be presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier
Notice within thirty days of receipt of information from the bank regarding return of cheque as unpaid, has to be served upon drawer, demanding payment of amount of money
on failure of drawer of such cheque to make payment within fifteen days of receipt of such notice, the payee or holder of cheque has to file complaint within one month thereof
All the above
questions.explanation: All three statements correctly reflect Sections 138 and 142 NI Act (as in force in 2015): presentation within six months/validity, notice within 30 days of return, and complaint within one month of expiry of the 15-day payment period.

questions.subject: Negotiable Instruments
questions.question: The delay in filing a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, can be condoned:
options: under Section 5 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1963
under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
under Section 142 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
under Section 143 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
questions.explanation: The proviso to Section 142(b) NI Act (added in 2002) empowers the court to condone delay in filing a Section 138 complaint if sufficient cause is shown; condonation is thus under Section 142, not Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
questions.reference: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, Section 142(b), Section 138, Section 142

questions.subject: Information Technology Act
questions.question: In which of the following judgments has the Supreme Court struck down Section 66-A of t
options: Shreya singhal vs. Union of India - AIR 2015 SC 1523
Selvi and others Vs. State of Karnataka - (2010) 7 SCC 263
PUCL Vs. Union of India - (1997) 1 SCC 301
Amar singh vs. Union of India - (2011) 7 SCC 67
questions.explanation: Section 66-A of the IT Act, 2000 was struck down as unconstitutional in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, AIR 2015 SC 1523 / (2015) 5 SCC 1.
questions.reference: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, (2015) 5 SCC 1; IT Act, Section 66A
questions.note: The stem ends mid-phrase in the PDF. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: POCSO
questions.question: According to Section 25 of the Protection of children from Sexual offences Act, 2012, statement of a child under Section 164 of the code of Criminal Procedure to be recorded by the Magistrate:-
options: shall be recorded in presence of the advocate of the accused
shall not be recorded in presence of the advocate of the accused
shall be recorded in presence of the Investigating Officer
Shall be recorded in presence of woman Police officer
questions.explanation: Section 25 POCSO Act, 2012 requires the Magistrate recording the child's statement under Section 164 CrPC to do so as far as practicable in the presence of the parents/person trusted by the child, and it shall not be recorded in the presence of the accused's advocate.
questions.reference: POCSO Act, Sections 25 and 26; CrPC, Section 164
questions.note: The supplied explanation mixes provisions on statements before a Magistrate and additional safeguards. PDF answer key: B.

questions.subject: Probation of Offenders
questions.question: Which of the following is not the duty of a Probation officer?
options: To supervise probationers placed under his supervision and where necessary, endeavour to find them suitable employment
To advise and assist offenders in payment of compensation or costs ordered by the court
To inquire into the circumstances or home surroundings of any person accused of an offence
To arrange for lodging and boarding of the probationers
questions.explanation: The duties of a probation officer (Section 14, Probation of Offenders Act, 1958) include inquiry into circumstances, supervision and assistance with employment, and advising on compensation/costs. Arranging lodging and boarding of probationers is not a statutory duty, so (d) is not a duty.

questions.subject: POCSO
questions.question: Which of following conditions, as per provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, 2012, has to be adhered to while examining or recording statement of the child:
options: the statement of child shall be recorded at the residence of child or the place where he usually resides or the place of his choice
as far as practicable the statement should be recorded by woman police officer not below the rank of Sub Inspector, who shall not be in uniform
the Investigating officer shall ensure that at no point of time the child comes in contact in any way with the accused
all the above
questions.explanation: Sections 24 & 26 POCSO Act, 2012 require all these safeguards: statement at child's residence/place of choice, recording by a woman SI not in uniform as far as practicable, and ensuring no contact with the accused. Hence 'all the above'.
questions.reference: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Sections 24

questions.subject: Information Technology Act
questions.question: A private key and its mathematically related public key, which are so related that the public key, can verify a digital signature created by the private key. in an Asymmetric crypto system means:-
options: Key pair
Both keys
Soft keys
soft pair
questions.explanation: Section 2(1)(x) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 defines 'key pair' in an asymmetric crypto system as a private key and its mathematically related public key that can verify a digital signature created by the private key.

questions.subject: Information Technology Act
questions.question: A person, who sends, generates, stores or transmits any electronic message; or causes any electronic message to be sent, generated, stored or transmitted to any other person, is called:
options: Sender
originator
Generator
Intermediary
questions.explanation: Section 2(1)(za) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 defines 'originator' as a person who sends, generates, stores or transmits any electronic message (or causes it), excluding an intermediary.

questions.subject: Electricity Act
questions.question: What is the minimum and maximum sentence that can be awarded to an accused guilty of second or subsequent offence of theft of electric lines and materials under Section 136 of the Electricity Act, 2003:
options: not less than 1 year but which may extend to 10 years and also fine which shall not be less than one lac rupees
not less than 6 months but which may extend to 5 years and also fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees
not less than 3 months but which may extend to 3 years and also fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees
not less than 9 months but which may extend to 3 years and also fine which shall not be less than one lac rupees
questions.explanation: Section 136(1) proviso, Electricity Act, 2003: for a second/subsequent conviction for theft of electric lines/materials, imprisonment shall not be less than six months extendable to five years, with fine not less than ten thousand rupees.

questions.subject: Information Technology Act
questions.question: A police officer empowered to investigate cyber crime as per Section 78 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, must not be below the rank of
options: Sub Inspector
Inspector
Deputy Superintendent of Police
Superintendent of Police
questions.explanation: Section 78 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (as amended 2008) empowers a police officer not below the rank of Inspector to investigate offences under the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: In which of the following judgments did the Supreme Court set aside the judgement of the High Court of Delhi which decriminalised Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860:
options: Sakshi vs. Union of India - AIR 2004 SC 3566
Naz Foundation (India) Trust vs. Suresh Kumar Koushal - (2014) 3 SCC 220
PUCL Vs. Union of India - (2010) 14 SCC 245
Suresh Kumar Kaushal vs. Naz Foundation (India) Trust (2014) 1 SCC 1
questions.explanation: In Suresh Kumar Koushal v. Naz Foundation, (2014) 1 SCC 1, the Supreme Court set aside the Delhi High Court's Naz Foundation judgment and upheld/reinstated Section 377 IPC. Option (b) inverts the cause-title, so (d) is correct.
questions.reference: Suresh Kumar Koushal v. Naz Foundation, (2014) 1 SCC 1
questions.note: Historical case-identification question. Read alongside Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India for subsequent treatment of Section 377.

questions.subject: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
questions.question: Which of the following acts constitute 'Atrocity' as defined in Section 3(1) of the scheduled Castes and scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
options: Forcing to drink or eat any inedible or obnoxious substances
Intentionally insulting or intimidating with intent to humiliate in any place within public view
Forcing or intimidating not to vote or to vote for a particular candidate or vote in a manner other than provided by law
All the above
questions.explanation: All three acts (forcing inedible substances, intentional insult in public view, and intimidation regarding voting) are enumerated atrocities under Section 3(1) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
questions.reference: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Section 3(1)

questions.subject: NDPS Act
questions.question: Benefit of probation to a convict of offence under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic substances Act, 1985 can be provided only if:
options: he is under 21 years of age and is convicted for offence punishable under Section 26 or 27 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
he is under 18 years of age or is convicted for offence punishable under Section 26 or 27 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
to any accused, regardless of his age, sentenced to rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years
none of the above
questions.explanation: Section 33 NDPS Act, 1985 bars probation (CrPC §360/Probation of Offenders Act) for NDPS convicts UNLESS the person is under eighteen years of age OR the offence is punishable under Section 26 or 27. Option (b) matches ('under 18 OR §26/27').
questions.reference: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, Section 33, Section 26

questions.subject: Juvenile Justice
questions.question: Who, as per Section 2(1) of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of children) Act, 2000, is a 'Juvenile in conflict with law'?
options: A Juvenile who is alleged to have committed an offence and has not completed eighteen years of age as on the date of commission of such offence
A Juvenile who is alleged to have committed an offence and has not completed twelve years of age on the date of commission of such offence
A Juvenile who is alleged to have committed an offence and has not completed sixteen years of age on the date of commission of such offence
A Juvenile who is alleged to have committed an offence and has not completed fourteen years of age on the date of commission of such offence
questions.explanation: Section 2(l) of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 defines a 'juvenile in conflict with law' as one who has not completed eighteen years of age as on the date of commission of the offence.
questions.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, Section 2(l)

questions.subject: Juvenile Justice
questions.question: Which of the following statements is not correct:
options: one or more Juvenile Justice Boards shall be constituted by the State Government for every district
each Juvenile Justice Board shall consists of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate and two social workers, of whom at least one shall be a woman
the order passed by the Juvenile Justice Board in absence of any Member at any stage of proceedings shall be invalid

power of the Juvenile Justice Board may also be exercised by the High Court and the court of Sessions when Court and the Court of Sessions, when the proceedings come before them in appeal, revision or otherwise
questions.explanation: Under Section 4(3) proviso of the JJ Act, 2000, an order passed by the Board in the absence of any member at any stage of proceedings shall NOT be invalid merely on that ground. So the statement in (c) is the incorrect one.
questions.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, Section 4(3)

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 32 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, statement of a person, who is dead, is relevant:
options: if it relates to cause of someone else's death
if it relates to cause of his own death or someone else's death
if it relates to the cause of his own death
none of the above
questions.explanation: Section 32(1) of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (dying declaration) makes a deceased's statement relevant when it relates to the cause of his own death or circumstances of the transaction resulting in his death; it concerns his OWN death.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Section 436-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, provides for grant of bail to an accused pending trial if:
options: he has undergone detention for one-fourth period of imprisonment specified for the offence for which he is being tried
/he has undergone detention for one-third period of imprisonment specified for the offence for which he is being tried
he has undergone detention for one-half period of imprisonment specified for the offence for which he is being tried
(a) and (b) above
questions.explanation: Section 436-A CrPC, 1973 entitles an under-trial to release on bail once he has undergone detention up to one-half of the maximum imprisonment specified for the offence.

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: Facts, which, though not in issue, are so connected with a fact in issue as to form part of the same transaction, whether they occurred at the same time and place or at different times and places:
options: are irrelevant
are relevant
are partly relevant
none of the above
questions.explanation: Section 6 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (res gestae): facts forming part of the same transaction as a fact in issue are relevant, whether occurring at the same or different times and places.

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: Which of the following statements, as per provisions of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, is not correct?
options: Facts which are inconsistent with any fact in issue, shall not be relevant

Facts not otherwise relevant are relevant if by themselves or in connection with other facts, they make the existence or non-existence of any fact in issue or relevant fact highly probable or improbable
Any fact is relevant, which shows or constitutes a motive or preparation for any fact in issue or relevant fact
Admissions are not conclusive proof of the matters admitted, but they may operate as estoppels under the provisions of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872
questions.explanation: Under Section 11 of the Evidence Act, facts inconsistent with any fact in issue ARE relevant. So statement (a) ('shall not be relevant') is the incorrect one.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Narcoanalysis, polygraph test and brain electrical activation profile test conducted against will of the person subjected to such tests, violates his right protected under Article 20(1), and right to personal liberty protected under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, was held by the Supreme Court in which of the following cases:
options: Wakkar and Another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh - (2011) 3 SCC 306
Munna Kumar Upadhyay vs. State of Andhra Pradesh - (2012) 6 SCC 174
Jagroop singh vs. State of Punjab - (2012) 11 scc 768
Selvi and others vs. State of Karnataka - (2010) 7 SCC 263
questions.explanation: In Selvi v. State of Karnataka, (2010) 7 SCC 263, the Supreme Court held that involuntary narcoanalysis, polygraph and BEAP tests violate Article 20(3) and Article 21 of the Constitution.
questions.reference: Selvi v. State of Karnataka, (2010) 7 SCC 263; Constitution, Articles 20(3) and 21
questions.note: The stem cites Article 20(1), while the explanation cites Article 20(3). PDF answer key: D.

questions.subject: Rajasthan General Rules (Criminal)
questions.question: Statement 'A' - when a court of Sessions passes a sentence of death, the court shall, according to Rule 102 of the General Rules (Criminal) 1980, commit the prisoner by a warrant in the appropriate form to the jail from which he came to stand his trial, and shall submit its proceedings to the High Court at the latest on the fourth day after the sentence of death has been pronounced. Statement 'B' - when a court of Sessions passes a sentence against a female prisoner to death, according to Rule 104 of the General Rules (criminal) 1980, it shall consider after enquiring from such prisoner herself, if necessary, whether she is pregnant and if it thinks that it is likely, it shall have her examined by the District Medical officer or such other doctor as it may consider fit and if it finds that she is in fact pregnant, it shall make a report to the High Court.
options: Both the aforesaid statements are correct
Statement 'A' is correct and Statement 'B' is incorrect
Statement 'B' is correct and Statement 'A' is incorrect
None of them is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements correctly reproduce Rules 102 and 104 of the Rajasthan General Rules (Criminal), 1980 regarding commitment of a death-sentenced prisoner and the enquiry into pregnancy of a female prisoner sentenced to death.

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: How many kinds of punishment are provided in Section 53 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860?
options: six
Four
Five
Seven
questions.explanation: Section 53 IPC provides five kinds of punishment: death, imprisonment for life, imprisonment (rigorous/simple), forfeiture of property, and fine.

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: According to Sections 73 and 74 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, a convict can be kept in solitary confinement for any portion or portions of imprisonment to which he is sentenced. Which of the following is incorrect?
options: For period not exceeding three months in the whole
For period not exceeding three months, if the term of the imprisonment exceeds six months and does not exceed one year
For period not exceeding three months if the term of imprisonment exceeds one year
The solitary confinement in no case shall exceed 14 days at a tim
questions.explanation: Section 73 IPC caps solitary confinement at a maximum of three months only where imprisonment exceeds one year; (c) omits the limit and states 'exceeds one year' without the three-month cap context wrongly, making it the incorrect statement (the correct scale: <=6m:1m; 6m-1yr:2m; >1yr:3m).
questions.note: The printed key labels as incorrect a choice that reproduces the three-month ceiling described by the solution. PDF answer key: C.

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: A knows Z to be behind a bush. B does not know it. A, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely to cause z's death, induces 8 to fire at the bush. B fires and kills z. What offence has been committed by A and B?
options: A and B both would be guilty of committing offence punishable under Section 302 IPC
while A would be guilty of committing offence under Section 302 IPC, B would be guilty of committing offence under Section 304 Part II, IPC,
A would be guilty of committing offence punishable under Section 302 IPC, B would be guilty of no offence
A and B both would be guilty of committing offence punishable under Section 304 Part-I of the IPC
questions.explanation: This is Illustration (b) to Section 299 IPC. A, intending/knowing Z's death likely, induces innocent B to fire; A is guilty of culpable homicide (Section 302/304), while B, having no knowledge, commits no offence.
questions.note: The stem has a corrupted actor label and the solution does not resolve the keyed offence uniquely. PDF answer key: C.

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: A is in a house which is on fire, with z, a child. People below hold out a blanket. A drops the child from the house-top, knowing it to be likely that the fall may kill the child but not intending to kill the child, and intending, in good faith, the child's benefit, and the child dies: Which of the following offences has been committed by A?
options: Section 304-A, of Indian Penal Code, 186
Section 304 part II, of Indian Penal Code, 1860
Section 302, of Indian Penal Code, 1860
A has committed no offence
questions.explanation: This is the illustration to Section 92 IPC (act done in good faith for another's benefit without consent in an emergency). A commits no offence.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the tense. I am pleading for the preservation of trees
options: simple Present Tense
Past Tense
Present continuous Tense
Past continuous Tense
questions.explanation: 'I am pleading' uses am + present participle (-ing), which is the Present Continuous Tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Fill in the blank with correct form of verb: My sister saw a snake while she ..................... in the garden
options: was walking
walks
Is walking
were walking
questions.explanation: A past action interrupted by another past action takes the past continuous: 'while she was walking in the garden.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Pick up the correct synonym for the word: STUBBORN
options: Easy
obstinate
willing
Pliable
questions.explanation: A synonym of 'stubborn' is 'obstinate.' Easy, willing and pliable are antonyms.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word opposite in the meaning to the word: ARBITRARY
options: Dictatorial
Autocratic
High handed
Methodical
questions.explanation: 'Arbitrary' (based on whim, not reason/order) is opposite to 'methodical' (orderly, systematic). The other options are synonyms.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom. 'A man of weight'
options: A fat person
To truthful and trustworthy man
A man of importance
A notorious man
questions.explanation: The idiom 'a man of weight' means a person of importance or influence.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom. 'A fool's paradise'
options: Paradise of idiots
A state of happiness for foolish reasons
To live in the past
To remain in the state of daydreaming
questions.explanation: The idiom 'a fool's paradise' means a state of happiness based on false hope or foolish/unfounded reasons. Option (b) captures this; daydreaming (d) is a distractor.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech. The policeman said to us, where are you going'?
options: The Policeman asked to us where we are going.
The policeman told us where we were going.
The Policeman enquired where we were going.
The Policeman said where were we going
questions.explanation: An interrogative ('where are you going?') in indirect speech uses 'asked/enquired' with no inversion and tense back-shift: 'The Policeman enquired where we were going.' Option (a) wrongly keeps present tense and adds 'to'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech. Call the first witness', said the Judge.
options: The Judge asked for calling first witness.
The Judge commanded them to call the first witness.
The Judge said to call the first witness.
The Judge requested to call for first witness
questions.explanation: An imperative/command ('Call the first witness') is reported with 'commanded/ordered + object + to-infinitive': 'The Judge commanded them to call the first witness.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech. She said to me, "I shall play now."
options: she told me that she should play now.
she told me that she should play then.
She told me that she would play now.
She told me that she would play then.
questions.explanation: 'I shall play now' back-shifts to 'would play' and the adverb 'now' becomes 'then': 'She told me that she would play then.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice. Someone gave her a bulldog
options: She was given a bulldog
A bulldog was given to her by someone.
she has been given a bulldog
She is being given a bulldog by someone.
questions.explanation: 'Someone gave her a bulldog' converts to passive with the indirect object as subject: 'She was given a bulldog' (agent 'by someone' dropped as indefinite). This is the standard preferred passive.
questions.note: Options A and B are both grammatically valid passive constructions. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice. Mona was writing a letter to her father
options: A letter was written to her father by Mona.
A letter has been written to her father by Mona.
A letter was being written by Mona to her father.
A letter was written by Mona to her father.
questions.explanation: Past continuous active ('was writing') becomes past continuous passive 'was being written': 'A letter was being written by Mona to her father.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Fill in the blanks with the correct options. ............... rich should help ..............poor
options: A, a
The, a
The, an
The, the
questions.explanation: 'The' before an adjective denotes a class of people ('the rich', 'the poor'). Hence 'The rich should help the poor' - option (d).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option. .............. pupil should obey his teacher
options: A
The
An
X
questions.explanation: A singular countable noun used generically takes the indefinite article: 'A pupil should obey his teacher.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option. Kalidas is .............. Shakespeare of India.
options: a
an
the
X
questions.explanation: When a proper noun is used as a common noun to denote an outstanding example ('the Shakespeare of India'), the definite article 'the' is used.

questions.subject: Legal Maxims
questions.question: What do you mean by 'ACTUS CURIAE NEMINEM GRAVABIT'
options: A personal right of action dies with the person
The law holds no man responsible for the act of God
An act of the court shall prejudice no man
None
questions.explanation: The maxim 'actus curiae neminem gravabit' means 'an act of the court shall prejudice no man' - no party should suffer due to a mistake of the court.

questions.subject: Succession
questions.question: Under provisions of Indian Succession Act, 1925 probate cannot be granted to:
options: A married daughter
A minor son
Illegitimate child
Half brother
questions.explanation: Under the Indian Succession Act, 1925 (s.234 and related provisions), probate/letters of administration follow legitimate kindred; an illegitimate child is not recognised as kindred for grant of probate. A married daughter, minor son or half-brother can otherwise take a grant.
questions.note: The key and explanation conflict with the rule concerning a minor's eligibility for probate. PDF answer key: C.

questions.subject: Hindu Law
questions.question: Under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 who among the following cannot be adopted:
options: A Hindu
Already adopted child
A minor
An unmarried child
questions.explanation: Section 10 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 lists who may be adopted: the person must be a Hindu, not already adopted, not married (unless custom permits) and below 15 years. A child already adopted cannot be adopted again.
questions.reference: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, Section 10

questions.subject: Legal Services Authorities Act
questions.question: Which of the following is not a 'Public Utility Service' for the purpose of the Legal Services Authority Act, 1987:
options: Transport Service
Postal, Telegraph or Telephone Service
Insurance Service
Banking Services
questions.explanation: Section 22A of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 defines 'public utility service' to include transport, postal/telegraph/telephone, power/water, hospital and insurance services. Banking is not in the central statutory definition, so it is not a public utility service.

questions.subject: Limitation
questions.question: In a case where a party is added or substituted owing to assignment or devolution of any interest during the pendency of a suit, the suit shall as regards him, be deemed to have been instituted:
options: On the date the suit was instituted.
When he had a party.
On the date when the application for addition or substitution is made.
None of the above.
questions.explanation: Under Order XXII Rule 10 (read with the proviso to s.21/limitation principles) CPC, where a party is added or substituted on assignment or devolution of interest during a suit, the suit as regards him is deemed instituted on the date the suit was originally instituted (the relation-back principle).
questions.reference: Limitation Act, 1963, Section 21(2); CPC, Order XXII Rule 10

questions.subject: Motor Vehicles Act
questions.question: As per Schedule for compensation for third party fatal accidents under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 the amount of compensation arrived at, in consideration of the expenses, which a victim would have incurred, towards maintaining himself, had he been alive, shall be reduced
questions.explanation: Under the Second Schedule to s.163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, one-third (1/3) of the income is deducted towards the amount the deceased would have spent on maintaining himself had he been alive.
questions.note: Historical question on the former Section 163A and Second Schedule.

questions.subject: Registration
questions.question: For an instrument of gift of immovable property, under the Registration Act, 1908:
options: Registration is compulsory
Registration is optional
Registration is exempted
None of the above
questions.explanation: Under s.17 of the Registration Act, 1908 (read with s.123 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882), a gift of immovable property must be effected by a registered instrument; registration is compulsory.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Where the time limit of a lease is of a year or number of years, which is expressed to be determinable before its expiration, and the lease omits to mention at whose option it is so terminable, who shall have such option:
options: Lessee
Lessor
Transferor
None of the above
questions.explanation: Section 108(c) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 provides that where a lease for a year/years is determinable before expiry and the lease omits to mention at whose option, such option lies with the lessee.
questions.note: The choice is supported by Section 110 rather than the section cited in the source explanation. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: Legal Maxims
questions.question: The maxim 'Actus curiae neminem gravabit means
options: An act of the Court shall prejudice no man
The act of God does wrong to no one.
An act in law shall prejudice no man.
An act does not constitute guilt unless done with a guilty intention.
questions.explanation: 'Actus curiae neminem gravabit' means an act of the Court shall prejudice no man - no party should suffer for a mistake or delay attributable to the Court.

questions.subject: Statutory Interpretation
questions.question: Which of the following is not an internal aid to the construction or interpretation of statute:
options: Long Title of an Act.
Illustrations
Marginal Notes appended to a section.
Preamble of a statute
questions.explanation: Long title, marginal notes and preamble are internal aids to construction (parts of the statute). Illustrations, being explanatory of the section, are sometimes treated as internal aids too, but among the given options 'Illustrations' is the answer the paper treats as not an internal aid; the long title, marginal notes and preamble are the classic internal aids.
questions.note: The explanation acknowledges that the keyed choice can also be an internal aid. PDF answer key: B.

questions.subject: Muslim Law
questions.question: Iddat period, in case of a divorced woman, if she is subject to menstruation, means:
options: Three menstrual courses after the date of divorce
Six months period after the date of divorce
Nine menstrual courses after the date of divorce.
Nine months after the date of divorce.
questions.explanation: Under Muslim law (and the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986), iddat for a divorced woman subject to menstruation is three menstrual courses after the date of divorce.
questions.reference: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986, Section 2(b)

questions.subject: Rajasthan Agricultural Indebtedness
questions.question: For the purpose of Rajasthan Relief of Agricultural indebtedness Act, 1957, the term 'agriculture' does not include:
options: Horticulture
Breeding of cattle, camels, sheep or goats
Bee farming and collecting honey
Reserving land for fodder grazing or thatching grass.
questions.explanation: The definition of 'agriculture' in the Rajasthan Relief of Agricultural Indebtedness Act, 1957 includes horticulture, breeding of cattle/camels/sheep/goats and reserving land for fodder/grazing/thatching grass, but does NOT include bee farming and collecting honey.
questions.reference: Rajasthan Relief of Agricultural Indebtedness Act, 1957

questions.subject: Rajasthan Stamp Act
questions.question: Any person aggrieved by an order made by the Collector (Stamps) can apply for a revision under Section 65 of the Rajasthan Stamp Act, 1998, before:
options: Rajasthan High Court
Chief Controlling Revenue Authority
Inspector General of Stamps
State Government
questions.explanation: Section 65 of the Rajasthan Stamp Act, 1998 provides for revision by the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority; a person aggrieved by an order of the Collector (Stamps) applies to that authority.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The Supreme Court of India in the exercise of its jurisdiction may make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any case, such power is conferred by:
options: Article 141 of the Constitution of India.
Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
Article 32 of the Constitution of India.
Article 124 of the Constitution of India.
questions.explanation: Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass such decree or order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In which Judgement, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held Right to Privacy to be a Fundamental Right:
options: Subramanium Swamy vs. Union of India & Ors.
Lok Prahari vs. Union of India & Ors.
Justice Sunanda Bhandare Foundation vs. Union of India & Ors.
Justice K.S.Puttaswamy & Anr. vs. Union of India & Ors.
questions.explanation: In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017) 10 SCC 1, a nine-judge bench held that the right to privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21.
questions.reference: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India, (2017) 10 SCC 1

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Which of the following is a valid defence against an action in tort:
options: Mistake of fact
Act of God
Minority
None of the above
questions.explanation: Act of God (vis major) is a recognised general defence in tort. Mistake of fact and minority are generally not valid defences in the law of torts.

questions.subject: Hindu Law
questions.question: When a marriage has been dissolved by a decree of divorce under Hindu Marriage Act,1955 and there is a right of appeal, the divorced persons may marry again:
options: After expiry of 1 month from the decree of divorce.
Immediately after passing of the decree of divorce.
After expiry of 2 months from the decree of divorce.
After expiry of the time for appealing, without any appeal having been presented.
questions.explanation: Section 15 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides that divorced persons may marry again after the time for appealing has expired without any appeal having been presented (or after dismissal of an appeal).

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: Promissory estoppel is the extension of principle contained in which provision of the Evidence Act:
options: Section 65
Section 110
Section 115
Section 150
questions.explanation: Promissory estoppel is an extension of the principle of estoppel contained in Section 115 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

questions.subject: Hindu Law
questions.question: Prior to the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 coming into force, who amongst the following was not Class I heir of male Hindu dying intestate:
options: Mother
Widow
Daughter
None of the above
questions.explanation: Mother, widow and daughter were all Class I heirs of a male Hindu dying intestate even prior to the 2005 amendment (Schedule, s.8 HSA, 1956). Hence none of them was excluded - 'None of the above'.
questions.reference: Hindu Succession Act, 1956, Section 8 and Schedule

questions.subject: Rajasthan Land Revenue
questions.question: Under which provision of Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956, a person without lawful authority occupying land, which is at the disposal of local authority, can be evicted:
options: Section 91 of the Act
Section 90-A of the Act
Section 90-B of the Act
Section 92 of the Act
questions.explanation: Section 91 of the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956 provides for summary eviction of a person occupying, without lawful authority, land which is at the disposal of the State or a local authority.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: 'Decree', as defined by Section 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 does not include:
options: A preliminary decree.
Rejection of a plaint.
Determination of any question within Section 144 CPC.
Any order of dismissal for default
questions.explanation: Section 2(2) CPC: 'decree' includes rejection of a plaint and determination of any question within s.144, and a preliminary decree, but expressly excludes any order of dismissal for default.
questions.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Section 2(2), s.144

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: Against a decree passed in a suit after recording a compromise, an appeal on the ground that the compromise should not have been recorded, can be filed under:
options: Section 151 CPC.
Order XXIII CPC.
Order XLIII Rule 1-ACPC.
None of the above.
questions.explanation: By the proviso to Order XXIII Rule 3 and Rule 3A CPC, no separate suit/appeal lies challenging a recorded compromise; the only remedy is before the same court that recorded it. No appeal under the listed provisions lies, so 'None of the above'. (Order XLIII Rule 1A only allows raising the validity of the compromise within the appeal against the decree itself, not as an independent appeal.)
questions.reference: CPC, Section 96(3), Order XXIII Rules 3 and 3A, and Order XLIII Rule 1A(2)
questions.note: The solution and the appeal provision cited within it require reconciliation. PDF answer key: D.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Rent Control
questions.question: Chapter II and III of Rajasthan Rent Control Act, 2001 applies to:
options: Any premises let out to a citizen of a foreign country.
Any premises belonging to or vested in a University established by any law for the time being in force.
Any premises belonging to a Government Company as defined under Section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956.
Any premises situated in the municipal area of Jaipur City, let out for residential purposes, for a monthly rent of Rs. 8,000/-.
questions.explanation: Section 3 of the Rajasthan Rent Control Act, 2001 exempts (excludes from Chapters II & III) premises let to foreign citizens, premises of a University/Government Company, etc. The Jaipur residential premises is the intended 'applies' answer (d). Flagged: per the bare Act, residential premises in Jaipur with rent of Rs.7,000 or more are also exempt, so Rs.8,000/month would arguably be exempt too - option appears internally inconsistent, but (d) is the official-key answer.
questions.note: The supplied explanation identifies a possible statutory exemption for the keyed premises. PDF answer key: D.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Municipal Law
questions.question: A suit against a municipality or its officers can be instituted otherwise than for the recovery of immovable property or for a declaration of title thereto:
options: After six months of the accrual of cause of action
After eight months of the accrual of cause of action.
Within six months next after the accrual of cause of action.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Suits against a municipality/its officers (other than for recovery of immovable property or declaration of title) must be instituted within six months next after the accrual of the cause of action (standard municipal-law limitation/notice provision).

questions.subject: Easements
questions.question: The grant of and transfer of licences is governed by:
options: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882.
The Specific Relief Act, 1963.
The Indian Contract Act, 1932.
The Indian Easements Act, 1882.
questions.explanation: Licences are dealt with under the Indian Easements Act, 1882 (ss.52-64); the grant and transfer of licences is governed by that Act.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Court Fees
questions.question: Under Rajasthan Court fees and Suits. Valuation Act, 1961, all questions arising on a plea that the subject matter of the suit has not been properly valued or that the fee paid is not sufficient, are required to be heard and decided:
options: At the final hearing of the suit.
At the discretion of the trial court.
Before the hearing of the suit as contemplated by Order XVIII CPC.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Under the Rajasthan Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1961, all questions on under-valuation or insufficiency of court-fee are to be heard and decided before the hearing of the suit (as contemplated by Order XVIII CPC).
questions.reference: Rajasthan Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1961

questions.subject: Specific Relief
questions.question: Which of the contract is not specifically enforceable:
options: A contract for the non performance of which compensation in money is not an adequate relief.
A contract which is in its nature determinable.
A contract, the performance of which does not involve the performance of a continuous duty, which the Court can supervise.
A contract which is not dependent on the personal qualification or volition of the parties.
questions.explanation: Under Section 14(1) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, a contract which is in its nature determinable cannot be specifically enforced. Options (a), (c) and (d) describe contracts that ARE specifically enforceable; (b) is the exception.

questions.subject: Rajasthan Tenancy
questions.question: The power of review on the Board of Revenue and other revenue courts is conferred by which provision of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955:
options: Section 207
Section 224
Section 229
Section 230
questions.explanation: Section 229 of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955 confers the power of review on the Board of Revenue and other revenue courts (Sections 229-231 deal with review, revision and reference).

questions.subject: Negotiable Instruments
questions.question: Which of the following is not a negotiable instrument:
options: Promissory note
Fixed Deposit Receipt
Bill of Exchange.
A cheque
questions.explanation: Section 13 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 recognises only promissory notes, bills of exchange and cheques as negotiable instruments. A Fixed Deposit Receipt is not a negotiable instrument.

questions.subject: Rajasthan General Rules (Civil)
questions.question: Under the General Rules (Civil), 1986 all pleadings, applications and petitions filed in the course of civil judicial proceedings, shall be written in:
options: Hindi
English
Any language specified in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Under the Rajasthan General Rules (Civil), 1986, pleadings, applications and petitions in civil judicial proceedings are required to be written in Hindi (the language of the courts in Rajasthan).

questions.subject: Arbitration
questions.question: Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, in the case of international commercial arbitration 'Court' means
options: The principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction.
Small Causes Court
The High Court
None of the above
