questions.explanation: Under Section 2(1)(e)(ii) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, in the case of international commercial arbitration 'Court' means the High Court in exercise of its ordinary original civil jurisdiction (or having jurisdiction to decide the questions forming the subject-matter).

questions.subject: Arbitration
questions.question: An order refusing to refer the parties to arbitration under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is appealable under:
options: Section 34 of the Act
Article 227 of the Constitution of India
Section 37 of the Act
Section 11 of the Act
questions.explanation: Section 37(1)(a) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 makes an order refusing to refer the parties to arbitration under Section 8 appealable. (Post the 2015 amendment Section 37 expressly covers refusal under Section 8.)
questions.reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 37(1)(a), Section 8, Section 37

questions.subject: Rajasthan Panchayati Raj
questions.question: The provisions for removal and suspension of any member or Chairperson of a Panchayati Raj Institution under the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 are contained in:
options: Section 119 of the Act
Section 38 of the Act
Section 117-A of the Act
Section 39 of the Act
questions.explanation: Section 38 of the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 contains the provisions for removal and suspension of any member, Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson of a Panchayati Raj Institution.

questions.subject: Partnership
questions.question: Under section 10 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 every partner is under a duty:
options: To render true accounts and full information.
To indemnify the firm for any loss caused to it by his fraud in the conduct of the business of the firm.
Not to carry on any business other than that of the firm.
To be just and faithful to each other.
questions.explanation: Section 10 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 ('Duty to indemnify for loss caused by fraud') casts on every partner the duty to indemnify the firm for any loss caused to it by his fraud in the conduct of the business of the firm. The other duties fall under Sections 9, 11 and 16.

questions.subject: Sale of Goods
questions.question: Under Sale of Goods Act, 1930, movable goods does not include:
options: Stock and shares
Grass
Money
Growing crops
questions.explanation: Under Section 2(7) of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, 'goods' means every kind of movable property other than actionable claims and money, but includes stock and shares, growing crops, grass, and things attached to land agreed to be severed. Money is expressly excluded.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: In a suit against a Corporation, the summons may be served on:
options: Any employee of the corporation
Relative of the director of the corporation.
Principal officer of the corporation.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Under Order XXIX Rule 2 CPC, in a suit against a corporation the summons may be served on the secretary, or on any director or other principal officer of the corporation.
questions.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order XXIX Rule 2

questions.subject: Information Technology Act
questions.question: The offences under Sections 66B, 66C, 66D and 66E of Information and Technology Act, 2000, are
options: Cognizable
Sessions Triable
Non-bailable
None of the above
questions.explanation: By virtue of Section 77B of the Information Technology Act, 2000, offences punishable with imprisonment of three years and above (which includes Sections 66B, 66C, 66D, 66E) are cognizable; these are bailable and not sessions-triable.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: A complainant, of a Magistrate triable case instituted upon a complaint, can challenge the judgement of acquittal passed by the competent court, by filing:
options: Revision in the Sessions Court.
Revision in the High Court.
Appeal before a Sessions Court.
Application for grant of leave to appeal in the High Court
questions.explanation: Under Section 378(4) CrPC, in a complaint case where the order is one of acquittal, the complainant may present an appeal to the High Court only after obtaining special leave to appeal from the High Court.

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: An information, supplied by an accused under Section 27 of the Evidence Act, shall be recorded:
options: In presence of two independent Panch witnesses.
In presence of a Gazetted Officer.
In presence of two Police Officers.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Section 27 of the Evidence Act prescribes no particular mode/witnesses for recording the information leading to discovery; the law mandates no presence of panch witnesses, Gazetted Officer or police officers as a condition. Hence 'None of the above.'

questions.subject: Juvenile Justice
questions.question: While assessing age of a person under the Juvenile Justice (care and protection of children) Act, 2015, the Court/Board is required to consider the documents/evidence in the following order of preference:
options: (i) Birth Certificate issued by a Municipality. (ii) School Certificate. (iii) Ossification test report. (iv) Aadhar Card.
(i) Ossification test report. (ii) Birth Certificate issued by the Municipality. (iii) Aadhar Card.
(i) Birth Certificate issued from the school/matriculation certificate. (ii) Date of birth certificate issued by the Municipality. (iii) Ossification test report.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Section 94(2) of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 prescribes the order of preference: (i) date of birth certificate from school / matriculation certificate; failing which (ii) birth certificate from a municipality/corporation; and only in absence of both, (iii) ossification/age determination test.
questions.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, Section 94(2)

questions.subject: Juvenile Justice
questions.question: Which of the following orders may not be passed by the Juvenile Justice Board after conducting inquiry of a child in conflict with law:
options: Direct the child to attend a school.
Direct the child to attend a vocational training centre.
Sentence the child to imprisonment till he attains 18 years of age.
Direct the child to perform community service.
questions.explanation: Under Section 18 of the JJ Act, 2015, the Board can pass dispositional orders (attend school, vocational training, community service, etc.) but cannot sentence a child in conflict with law to imprisonment; Section 21 bars death penalty/life imprisonment, and the Board has no power to imprison.
questions.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, Section 18, Section 21

questions.subject: Juvenile Justice
questions.question: A Children Court trying a child in conflict with law for a heinous offence, is not empowered to
options: Hold trial of a child as an adult.
Hold inquiry of the child as a Juvenile Justice Board.
Sentence the child to imprisonment for a term of 10 years.
Send the child to a place of safety till he attains the age of 21 years.
questions.explanation: Under Section 19 r/w Section 21 of the JJ Act, 2015, a Children's Court trying a child as an adult cannot sentence the child to imprisonment (death penalty/life imprisonment without release are barred and ordinary imprisonment is not the prescribed mode); a fixed-term sentence such as 10 years' imprisonment is impermissible.
questions.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, Section 19, Section 21
questions.note: The supplied explanation generalises the statutory sentencing restriction. Verify the distinction between a sentence and where it is served. PDF answer key: C.

questions.subject: Juvenile Justice
questions.question: Where, after inquiry under Section 15 of the Juvenile Justice (care and protection of children) Act, 2015, the Juvenile Justice Board is satisfied that a child above 16 years of age, has committed a heinous offence and should be tried as an adult, it may:
options: Commit the case to the Sessions Court concerned for trial of the child as an adult.
Try the child as per the procedure provided in Cr.P.C
Return the charge-sheet to the Investigating Officer for presentation in the Court concerned.
Transfer the case to the Children Court for trial of the child as an adult.
questions.explanation: Under Section 15 r/w Section 18(3) of the JJ Act, 2015, where the Board finds the child should be tried as an adult, it transfers the case to the Children's Court having jurisdiction to try such offences.
questions.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, Section 15, Section 18(3)

questions.subject: NDPS Act
questions.question: A private vehicle proceeding on a Highway, suspected to be carrying psychotropic drugs, may be searched by:
options: A Head Constable posted in the Police Station concerned.
A Sub-Inspector posted in some other District.
The Deputy Superintendent of Police or officer-in-charge of the police station of the area concerned.
All of the above
questions.explanation: Under Section 42 of the NDPS Act, 1985 (search of a vehicle in transit/conveyance on a highway falls under Section 43 for public place; empowered officers under Section 42 are the Deputy Superintendent of Police or officer-in-charge of the police station/empowered gazetted officers of the area concerned).
questions.reference: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, Section 42, Section 43
questions.note: The explanation gives conflicting statutory grounds for the vehicle search. PDF answer key: C.

questions.subject: NDPS Act
questions.question: Before searching a suspect carrying a bag containing narcotic drugs in his hand, the Officer concerned is required to apprise him of his right to be searched in the presence of:
options: A Magistrate or a Gazetted Officer.
Two independent witnesses from the locality.
Officer-in-charge of the Police Station of the area concerned.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Under Section 50 of the NDPS Act, 1985, before a personal search the officer must apprise the suspect of his right to be searched in the presence of a Gazetted Officer or a Magistrate (as held in State of Punjab v. Baldev Singh).
questions.reference: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, Section 50
questions.note: The question describes a bag search, while the explanation addresses a personal search. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: NDPS Act
questions.question: A vehicle, container or a receptacles used for commission of an offence punishable under the NDPS Act, 1985, shall not be liable to be confiscated:
options: If the person using the same is acquitted by the Court after trial.
If the prosecution fails to lead evidence about its ownership.
If the owner proves that the vehicle was used in commission of the offence without his knowledge or connivance.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Under the proviso to Section 60(3) of the NDPS Act, 1985, a conveyance shall not be confiscated if the owner proves that it was used in the commission of the offence without his knowledge or connivance and that he had taken reasonable precautions.
questions.reference: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, Section 60(3)

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: A being the owner of a plot of land, sells the same to B through a registered sale deed in the year 2005. B however does not make full payment to A. A again sells the same land to C in the year 2010 without informing him of the earlier transaction of 2005. Who would be the person aggrieved in these circumstances:
options: B (the first purchaser).
A (the seller).
C (the subsequent purchaser)
None of the above
questions.explanation: Under Section 27 r/w Section 19(b) of the Specific Relief Act, the prior registered sale to B (whether or not fully paid) creates a transfer; C, who paid value without notice of the earlier transaction, is the person aggrieved/prejudiced by A's fraudulent second sale.
questions.reference: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Section 27, Section 19(b)

questions.subject: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
questions.question: The bail application rejected by the Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, in a case involving offences under the said Act, may be challenged in the High Court, by filing:
options: Bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
Revision under Section 397 Cr.P.C.
Petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
An appeal
questions.explanation: Section 14A of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 provides an appeal to the High Court against an order granting or refusing bail by the Special Court; hence the rejection is challenged by way of an appeal (not Section 439/397/482 CrPC).
questions.reference: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Section 14A, Section 439

questions.subject: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
questions.question: X knows that Y is a member of the Scheduled Caste community. During the course of a free fight, X inflicts a grievous injury to Y by a sharp weapon. X is guilty of offence punishable under Section(s):
options: 326 IPC only
3(b)(V) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
326 IPC and 3(b)(V) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
None of the above
questions.explanation: In a free fight, the grievous hurt by sharp weapon is punishable under Section 326 IPC; the SC/ST Act offence under Section 3 requires the act to be committed 'on the ground that' the victim is a member of a SC/ST. In a free fight that caste-based intent is absent, so only Section 326 IPC applies.
questions.reference: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Section 326, Section 3
questions.note: Verify the version of the SC/ST Act applicable to this question. The interpretation in the solution is version-sensitive. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: A woman aged 30 years and her son aged 14 years, are witnesses to a murder. Their statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C. may be recorded by the Police Officer concerned at:
options: The scene of the occurrence.
The Women Police Station.
At the Police Station where FIR is registered.
The place where, such woman and her son reside
questions.explanation: Section 161 CrPC permits the police officer to examine and record statements of witnesses, including a woman and a child, at the scene of occurrence (or wherever the witness is found); there is no statutory bar requiring a particular police station or residence, so the statement may be recorded at the scene of occurrence.
questions.note: The explanation does not address the separate attendance protections in Section 160. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: In which of the following cases, the Court is required to record evidence before framing of charge:
options: Summons trial cases.
Sessions trial cases.
Warrant cases instituted upon a complain
Warrant cases instituted upon a Police report.
questions.explanation: Under Section 244 CrPC, in a warrant case instituted upon a complaint the Magistrate must take all such evidence as may be produced in support of the prosecution before framing of charge (Section 246). In police-report warrant cases (Section 240) and Sessions trials, charge is framed on the record/documents without pre-charge evidence.
questions.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Section 244, Section 246, Section 240

questions.subject: Domestic Violence Act
questions.question: Noncompliance of, which of the following orders passed under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, is an offence:
options: Maintenance order
Custody order
Residence order
Protection order
questions.explanation: Under Section 31 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, breach of a 'protection order' (or interim protection order) is the only non-compliance made a punishable offence (up to 1 year/Rs.20,000).
questions.reference: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Section 31

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: A woman subjected to rape, gives a statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. implicating the accused for the offence. She commits suicide sometime later but before her statement could be recorded at the trial. Such statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. would be:
options: Admissible as a substantive piece of evidence
Admissible under Section 32 of the Evidence Act.
Admissible under Section 33 of the Evidence Act.
Inadmissible in evidence.
questions.explanation: Once the maker is dead, her Section 164 CrPC statement as to the cause/circumstances of her death (rape leading to suicide) becomes admissible as a dying declaration under Section 32(1) of the Evidence Act; it is not 'substantive' evidence in the ordinary sense nor admissible under Section 33 (which needs prior cross-examination).
questions.reference: Indian Evidence Act, 1872, Section 32(1); CrPC, Section 164

questions.subject: Probation of Offenders
questions.question: A Court after holding trial, convicts and grants benefit of Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 to an accused. Which of the following orders is impermissible in law:
options: Admonish the offender.
Direct under Section 12 of the Act that the conviction shall not have an adverse effect on his service.
Direct the offender to pay compensation and cost.
Direct the offender to furnish bail and bonds to keep peace and good behaviour for three years.
questions.explanation: Close call. On grant of probation under Section 4 POA the offender executes a bond to appear and receive sentence and to keep peace/good behaviour up to 3 years, so a separate direction to furnish 'bail and bonds to keep peace and good behaviour for three years' (a CrPC Ch.VIII security measure) is the order that does not fit the POA scheme; admonition (s.3), removal of disqualification (s.12) and compensation/costs (s.5) are all permissible.
questions.reference: Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, Section 4, s.3, s.12
questions.note: The explanation identifies a possible conflict between the keyed order and the statutory probation bond. PDF answer key: D.

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: Two friends A and B were sleeping in a room which was bolted from inside. In the morning, A is found murdered. Under which provision of the Evidence Act, prosecution can claim shifting of burden on B to prove the manner in which the murder took place:
options: Section 114 of the Evidence Act.
Section 103 of the Evidence Act.
Section 106 of the Evidence Act.
Section 101 of the Evidence Act
questions.explanation: Where two persons are in a room bolted from inside and one is found murdered, the fact of how the death occurred is within the special knowledge of the survivor; burden to explain shifts to him under Section 106 of the Evidence Act.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: An FIR in relation to the offence under Section 406 IPC is lodged on 1.1.2010. The Police conducts investigation and submits a negative Final Report in the Court concerned on 2.2.2012. The Court takes cognizance of the above offence on 3.3.2013. In these circumstances, which of the following is correct
options: The proceedings are barred by limitation.
The proceedings are not barred by limitation as the offence under Section 406 IPC is a continuing offence.
The proceedings are not barred by limitation as the FIR was lodged promptly.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Section 406 IPC (criminal breach of trust) is treated as a continuing offence; limitation under Section 468 CrPC therefore does not bar the proceedings (and Section 470/473 also save them), so the prosecution is not time-barred.
questions.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Section 406, Section 468, Section 470
questions.note: The solution's continuing-offence rationale requires verification independently of the case dates. PDF answer key: B.

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: C being the wife of B, has obtained a decree of separation from the competent Court but they are still living in the same premises. B subjects C to intercourse. Their neighbour A watches the act and files an FIR. Which preposition is correct in these circumstances:
options: B is guilty of the offence punishable under Section 376-B IPC.
B is not guilty of any offence because C continues to be his legally wedded wife.
A would be guilty of the offence punishable under Section 354-C IPC.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Where the wife is living separately under a decree of separation, sexual intercourse by the husband without her consent is an offence under Section 376-B IPC.
questions.note: The stem and explanation describe the separation circumstances differently. Check the historical IPC provision and cognizance rule. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: 5 persons take illegal possession of a field. The owner (the complainant party) of the field collects his supporters and goes to the field for oust the trespassers therefrom. In the free fight, which ensues, the trespassers kill one person from the complainant's side. All The accused can be convicted :
options: With the aid of section 34 of IPC.
With the aid of section 149 of IPC.
For the individual injuries caused to the members of the complainant party.
None of the above
questions.explanation: In a sudden 'free fight' there is neither common intention (s.34) nor common object (s.149); each combatant is liable only for the individual injuries he personally caused.

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: The Investigating Officer conducting investigation of a case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 collects the call details of the mobile phones held by the accused from whom recovery of drug was effected and the conspirator, who supplied the drug. Such call details:
options: Can be used as substantive evidence to prove the charge of conspiracy
Are inadmissible in evidence
Can be considered relevant only if the conversation held between
None of the above
questions.explanation: Call detail records (electronic records) are admissible and, proving contact/association between the recovered-from accused and the supplier-conspirator, can be used as substantive evidence to establish the charge of conspiracy.
questions.note: The explanation does not address the conditions for proving electronic records. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: In a case involving the offence punishable under Section 304 Part II of IPC, the accused is arrested and the prosecution fails to comply with the requirements of Section 167(2) Cr.P.C. The accused, who is a habitual offender, becomes entitled to compulsive bail on:
options: 61st day from the date of his arrest.
91st day from the date of his arrest.
The accused is not entitled to be released on compulsive bail .
None of the above
questions.explanation: Section 304 Part II IPC carries imprisonment up to 10 years (not 10 years or more), so the default-bail period under the proviso to Section 167(2) CrPC is 60 days; the accused becomes entitled to compulsive bail on the 61st day, and habitual-offender status is irrelevant to the statutory right.
questions.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Section 304, Section 167(2)

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: A Patwari while preparing a revenue record, intentionally enters incorrect facts in the documents and signs & certifies the same with the intention of causing loss to the true owner of the land. The Patwari is guilty of:
options: Offence of creating false/ forged documents punishable under Sections 467 and 468 IPC.
Offence of using a forged document punishable under Section 471 IPC.
Offence of criminal breach of trust punishable under Section 406 IPC
None of the above
questions.explanation: A public servant (Patwari) who knowingly makes a false entry in a public/revenue record and certifies it to cause loss commits forgery of a record under Sections 467 and 468 IPC (Section 466 dealing with public records), i.e. creating false/forged documents.
questions.note: The explanation cites differing forgery provisions. Check the public-servant offence and the exact choices. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: Probation of Offenders
questions.question: An accused aged 20 years, having no previous criminal conduct, charged for the offence under Section 304 IPC, is convicted by the trial court. In these circumstances:
options: The trial court is under a mandate of law to release the accused on probation.
The trial court may release the accused on probation.
The accused is not entitled to the benefit of probation because the offence is punishable with imprisonment up to 10 years.
None of the above
questions.explanation: Section 304 IPC is not punishable with death or life imprisonment mandatorily, so it is not outside Section 4 POA; the court 'may' (discretionary, not mandatory) release a 20-year-old first offender on probation.
questions.reference: Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, Section 304, Section 4
questions.note: The stem does not identify the part of Section 304. That distinction can affect probation eligibility. PDF answer key: B.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: In which judgement, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down that a party, who is desirous of proving electronic evidence but does not have access to the device from which, the document was produced, is not required to produce and prove the certificate under Section 65-B of the Evidence Act:

questions.subject: Electricity Act
questions.question: A competent Court, shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under The Electricity Act, 2003:

Upon an oral complaint made by a Chief Electrical Inspector.
Upon a complaint in writing made by licencee or generating company
Upon none of the above

questions.subject: POCSO
questions.question: Under the provisions of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, can a report be published by the media, which discloses the identity of a sexually assaulted child:
